title: Resumable stream adapter: dual-mode AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams bridge with retryable resume
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Developers using the TypeScript SDK expect ergonomic streaming APIs that work both in browser and Node. We must provide a single surface that can be consumed as an AsyncIterator (for idiomatic TS/JS loops and server code) or as a Web ReadableStream (for browser-native piping and fetch response compatibility). Additionally, network/failure retries should be able to resume in-flight streams when feasible (e.g., reconnecting to a model stream and continuing from a checkpoint) without breaking backpressure semantics or leaking memory.

Goal: Design and implement a 'ResumableStreamHandle' abstraction that exposes both consumption modes, preserves precise cancellation/backpressure propagation, supports resumable retry semantics with an idempotency/resume token protocol, and provides clear examples for SDK users. Provide robust tests and a migration guide for existing consumers.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a single object that exposes asAsyncIterator() and asWebStream() with identical event ordering semantics
Cancellation in either mode propagates to runtime and frees buffers within 10ms under normal load
Retry/resume flow can reconnect and continue from last checkpoint when server returns a resume token; client-visible sequence continuity preserved
Examples for Node (AsyncIterator) and Browser (ReadableStream) added to docs and samples folder
Automated tests covering backpressure, cancellation, and resume logic in CI
Performance regression < 5% for common small-response workloads compared to current non-resumable streaming API
design_notes: High-level approach: implement a lightweight bridge that internally uses a single event source (a controlled queue) and exposes two adapters: an AsyncGenerator wrapper and a ReadableStream wrapper. Both adapters read from the same queue, but only one consumer is allowed per handle. This keeps ordering and buffering deterministic.

Resumable protocol: server emits explicit 'checkpoint' events with monotonically increasing checkpoint_id and optional byte/seq offsets. On transient failure, client requests resume with last_checkpoint_id and an idempotency token. Server validates and resumes from that checkpoint or rejects (in which case we fall back to full restart).

Backpressure model: the internal queue supports a configurable high-water mark. ReadableStream pull() invokes queue.consume(n) semantics to drain tokens; the AsyncIterator awaits queue.next(). Cancellation from either adapter calls handle.cancel(reason) which flushes queue and emits a final Cancelled error to the other adapter if attached.

Implementation detail: keep adapters lightweight (O(1) per token). Avoid copying token payloads between adapters; both adapters reference immutable event objects. We will cap maximum buffered events to avoid memory blowup (default 1024 events, configurable).

Edge cases: simultaneous open of both adapters should throw an error (we'll implement openMode enforcement). Reconnect/resume requires server support; fallbacks will be documented and surfaced via the SDK error type 'ResumeNotSupportedError' with troubleshooting guidance.

Trade-offs considered:
- Option A: independent streams with shared offset metadata (simpler but introduces reordering/race conditions)
- Option B (chosen): single authoritative queue + dual adapters (safer ordering, more predictable memory behavior, small added complexity).

Security/ops: resume tokens are short-lived single-use strings tied to a session. Tokens are encrypted on the server; client sends tokens over TLS only. We will add an opt-out flag for customers with strict audit requirements to disable resume (defaults to enabled).
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Initial RFC drafted; proposed ResumableStreamHandle with single-queue bridge. Shared with SDK and Runtime teams for feedback.

2026-03-11: Feedback from Runtime: server should emit checkpoint objects with checkpoint_id and optional model_kv_offset. Runtime owners agreed to add support in runtime-1.18 branch. Added dependency ENG-52210.
2026-03-12: Prototype adapter implemented in sdk/streaming/prototype. Basic AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream interop working in Node + Chrome (manual testing).
2026-03-13: Design review with DX and PM. Decided to default to 'resume: true' but expose resume:false in request config for customers. Added user-facing examples to docs PR draft.
2026-03-14: Opened feature branch feat/stream-resume and created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4232. Added unit tests for cancellation and basic resume handshake.
qa_checks: Unit tests: AsyncIterator consumer receives exactly same sequence as ReadableStream consumer for N=1000 events
Integration: simulate transient TCP reset and verify resume handshake succeeds when server supports checkpoint
Memory: run stress test with 100 concurrent streams for 30m and verify no unbounded buffer growth (max RSS delta < 200MB)
Backpressure: ensure high-throughput pipeline (1000 msgs/s) respects consumer speed limits and does not drop events
Browser compatibility: test in Chrome, Firefox, Safari + Node 18+ (native streams) and Node 14/16 with polyfills
followups: ENG-52001: Expose typed helpers for resume strategies (auto, manual, none)
ENG-52130: Console UX: surface stream resume events and token age in Trace view
ENG-52500: Docs: migration guide for existing streaming users to move to ResumableStreamHandle
